patient._comment: 'patient' contains the three sections that may be exposed in the detailed patient display: presentation, answer, and clinical.

presentation._comment: The immutable patient evidence package available for triage. Panel context controls whether other sections are locked or available.
presentation.quote: My head really hurts and the lights are too bright. My neck is stiff and I feel yucky. I got these little red dots on my legs that don't go away when you press them.
presentation.triageNote: 8-year-old female with high fever, severe headache, light sensitivity, neck stiffness, and a spreading non-blanching petechial rash. She is tachycardic and her blood pressure is 92/54.

answer._comment: The authoritative game answer. Explicit ESI, destination, and destination rationale are answer-bearing content; the player's assignment remains session state.
answer.destinationReason: ESI 2 is appropriate because a high-risk febrile illness with meningismus and a non-blanching petechial rash requires rapid isolation, resuscitative assessment, and empiric treatment.

clinical._comment: Display-ready clinical interpretation derived from patient.presentation. It preserves clinical meaning but must not explicitly name or identify the correct ESI level or destination; it does not participate in scoring.
clinical.summary: This child has high fever, severe headache, photophobia, neck stiffness, petechiae, tachycardia, and borderline blood pressure.
clinical.acuityReason: The non-blanching rash combined with meningismus may represent invasive bacterial infection; treatment cannot safely wait for diagnostic confirmation.
expectedResources: IV access, blood cultures, and laboratory testing
Lumbar puncture only when clinically safe
redFlags: Non-blanching petechiae with fever and meningismus
teachingPoints: Antibiotics should not be delayed for lumbar puncture when invasive bacterial infection is suspected.
A child can deteriorate rapidly before profound hypotension develops.

possibleDiagnoses: Viral meningitis with an unrelated rash
possibleClinicalOutcome.disposition: Immediate isolation, cultures, antibiotics, and hemodynamic support would be followed by hospital admission, potentially to intensive care.

aiImageGeneration._comment: 'aiImageGeneration' is info for AI to generate the image of the patient. Most images were done with openAI gpt-image-1 using an API, not the app, in July 2026. Look for some python scripts that are used to create these images. Be sure that the anchor-image is available and is provided to the AI - otherwise the images will not be consistent.
aiImageGeneration.who: white 8-year-old girl, clearly unwell, in an off-white t-shirt, charcoal shorts, and brown shoes
aiImageGeneration.pose: seated and slumped forward, one hand shielding her closed eyes from light
signs: many tiny, flat, pinpoint dark-red-to-purple petechiae scattered irregularly over both exposed lower legs
eyes squeezed shut with one hand shielding them from light
aiImageGeneration.prompt: Create a new square patient character asset for patient 026, closely matching the softly shaded painterly semi-realistic animated clinical-illustration style, lighting, rounded forms, fine outlines, and blue padded clinic chair of the attached references. IMPORTANT BACKGROUND REQUIREMENT: place the isolated patient and chair against a perfectly uniform, solid pure chroma-key green background (#00FF00), edge to edge. No gradient, texture, scenery, vignette, floor, cast shadow, green spill, or green clothing. The green will be removed to transparency later. The existing patient image is an identity/composition reference; correct its rash depiction. Show exactly one white 8-year-old girl in a plain off-white T-shirt, charcoal shorts, and brown shoes, seated on the chair in a full-body three-quarter front view with the entire head, body, hands, legs, shoes, and chair inside frame. She is clearly very ill: slumped and hunched forward, eyes squeezed shut, one hand shielding her eyes from bright light, face flushed, miserable and photophobic. On both exposed lower legs, show a clinically plausible sparse-to-moderate scattering of many tiny pinpoint dark-red-to-purple petechiae, mostly 1–3 mm dots, flat and non-raised in appearance, irregularly distributed, with a few small clustered areas. They must look like fine pinprick petechiae—not large round spots, hives, pustules, bruises, measles, chickenpox, or decorative polka dots. Keep the rash secondary to the patient, but clearly visible at normal viewing size. Natural anatomy: exactly two arms, two hands, two legs, two feet; no extra digits or limbs. No medical equipment, text, labels, or logos. Do not copy the cheerful expression or toy from the child style anchor.
